Great. Here’s a structured 12-week strength + hypertrophy programme tailored for a 26-year-old recreational lifter with no cycle-related contraindications, currently on combined OCP. The plan emphasizes progressive overload for strength and hypertrophy, with clear weekly structure, exercise selections, sets/reps, progression cues, and recovery/nutrition considerations. It assumes 4 training days per week, with optional accessory work and deloads built in. Dates can be aligned to 2026-06-01 as the start.

Overview
- Goals: increase maximal strength (SQ, BP, DL) and hypertrophy (major muscle groups) to improve body composition.
- Training days: 4 days per week (Total Body emphasis with upper/lower split within the 4-day window).
- Phases: 12 weeks split into 3x4-week blocks (Accumulate -> Intensify -> Peak/Consolidate).
- Progression: linear progression within each microcycle, with autoregulation and velocity-based cues if available.
- Accessory work: included to address symmetry, core stability, and hypertrophy.
- Recovery: emphasis on sleep (7–9 hours), protein ~1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, and nutrition timing around workouts. Deload week at end of Phase 2 or early Phase 3 if needed.

Assumptions
- Training days: Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri (example). Can shift by client schedule.
- Equipment: barbells, dumbbells, rack, bench, pulley/cables if available; substitutions provided.
- No injuries or contraindications beyond standard.

Phase 1: Accumulate (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish technique, build work capacity, start progressive overload, hypertrophy stimulus.

Weekly structure (example: Mon/Thu Lower/Upper, Tue/Fri Upper/Lower, or keep 4-day split depending on client setup)
Option A: 4-day alternating Upper/Lower
- Week 1–2: Focus on tempo and form; moderate volume.
- Week 3–4: Increase load modestly; maintain reps.

Week-by-week plan (Weeks 1–4)
Week 1 (Accumulation A)
- Day 1: Upper A
  - Barbell Back Squat (or Front Squat if preferred): 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Bench Press: 3x6
  - Bent-Over Barbell Row: 3x8
  - Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x10
  - Accessory: Face Pulls 3x12, Dumbbell Crowding Lateral Raises 2x12
  - Core: Plank 3x40s
- Day 2: Lower A
  - Deadlift (Conventional or RDL): 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Walking Lunges: 3x8 per leg
  - Leg Press or Front Squat: 3x10
  - Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust: 3x12
  - Calf Raises: 3x15
  - Core: Hanging Leg Raises 3x10
- Day 3: Upper B
  - Overhead Press or Push Press: 3x5
  - Incline Dumbbell Bench Press: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown or Pull-Ups: 3x8
  - Dumbbell Row: 3x10
  - Accessory: Tricep Pushdown 3x12, Dumbbell Curls 3x12
- Day 4: Lower B
  - Back Squat or Goblet Squat: 3x6
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Single-Leg Calf Raise: 3x12
  - Core: Pallof Press 3x12 per side

Notes Week 1–2: RPE targets around 7–8, not to failure. Use 2–3 minutes rest on big lifts, 60–90 seconds on assistance.

Week 2: Similar template with 2–3% load increase on main lifts if technique is solid and RPE ~7–8. Maintain volume.

Week 3 (Hypertrophy Focus)
- Increase total sets for upper body accessory work by 1–2 sets; keep main lifts at 3x5 or 3x6 with load ~77–80% 1RM.
- Add 1 extra set to accessory movements (e.g., 3x12 instead of 3x10).

Week 4 (Deload/Technique)
- Deload: reduce volume by 40–50% but keep movement quality. Main lifts at 60–65% 1RM for 3x5.

Phase 2: Intensify (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: shift toward higher intensity, slightly lower reps, greater strength emphasis while maintaining hypertrophy.

Week-by-week plan (Weeks 5–8)
Week 5 (Strength Emphasis)
- Day 1 Upper A
  - Barbell Back Squat: 4x4 at 80–85% 1RM (if lower body is primary, adjust to keep emphasis)
  - Bench Press: 4x4 at 80–85% 1RM
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x6
  - Accessory: Face Pulls 3x12, Hammer Curls 3x10
  - Core: Side Plank 3x30s per side
- Day 2 Lower A
  - Deadlift: 4x3–4 at 85% 1RM
  - Front Squat or Tempo Back Squat: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute Bridge/HP: 3x10
  - Calf Raises: 4x12
- Day 3 Upper B
  - Incline Barbell Press: 4x6
  - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 4x6–8
  - Seated Dumbbell Press: 3x8
  - Dumbbell Row: 3x8
  - Accessory: Tricep DSS 3x12, Cable Curls 3x12
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Squat variation: 4x5
  - Romanian Deadlift: 4x6
  - Walking Lunges: 3x8 per leg
  - Calf Raises: 4x12
  - Core: Pallof 3x12

Week 6 (Volume Increase)
- Similar to Week 5 but add 1–2 reps on main lifts where possible or add 1 accessory set per movement.

Week 7 (Mixed Intensity)
- 3-week ladder: 5x5 on primary lifts or 4x5 with slight deload in between if needed.
- Accessory work: maintain 3x8–12.

Week 8 (Deload)
- Reduce total volume by ~40% and reduce intensity to ~60–65% 1RM, maintain technique focus.

Phase 3: Peak/Consolidate (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: peak strength on key lifts, maintain or grow hypertrophy, refine body composition, prepare for potential testing.

Week 9 (Peaking Prep)
- Day 1 Upper A
  - Back Squat: 3–4x3 at 85–90% 1RM
  - Bench Press: 3–4x3 at 85–90% 1RM
  - Barbell Row: 3x5
  - Overhead Press: 3x5
  - Accessory: Tricep Pushdown 3x10, Dumbbell Curls 3x10
- Day 2 Lower A
  - Deadlift: 3x2–3 at 90% 1RM
  - Front Squat: 3x3
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6
  - Calf Raises: 4x10

Week 10 (Volume Retention)
- Similar to Week 9 but slightly lower weight to maintain form; 3–4 sets on principal lifts with 2–4 reps left in reserve.

Week 11 (Taper/Technique)
- Focus on technique and speed on main lifts.
- 2–3 sets of 2–3 reps at 90% of 1RM but with explosive intent.
- Accessory work reduced to maintain recovery.

Week 12 (Performance/Consolidation)
- Test or estimate 1RM for key lifts (if desired) with proper warm-up.
- 3–4 sets of 2–3 reps at heavy but controlled loads.
- Finish with light hypertrophy work to maintain muscle balance.

Sample daily breakdowns (concrete template)
- Day A: Upper
  - Main lift: choose between Barbell Back Squat or Bench Press depending on the day. If Upper, substitute lower body with Push-Pull emphasis.
  - Example: Bench Press 4x4; Barbell Row 4x6; Overhead Press 3x6; Incline Dumbbell Press 3x8; Pull-Ups 3x6–8; Accessory: Triceps/Curls 3x12
- Day B: Lower
  - Main lift: Deadlift or Squat variations; 3–4 sets
  - Accessories: Lunges, Glute/Ham raises, Calves, Core

Progression guidelines
- Load progression: aim to increase load whenever you can complete the prescribed reps with good form and RPE ~8–9 on main lifts.
- Volume adjustments: if technique falters or RPE drifts above target, reduce weight or add a deload week earlier.
- Reps vs. load: move up in load first, then adjust reps as needed to meet target zones.

Tempo, technique and cues
- Squat/Deadlift: controlled descent 2–3 seconds, explode up; depth to be below parallel for squats.
- Bench: feet planted, scapular retraction, bar path vertical; touch at mid-chern.
- Overhead press: controlled ascent, avoid hyperextension.
- Row/Pull: scapular retraction, horizontal pull.

Recovery and nutrition
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 3–5 meals; include post-workout protein (20–40 g).
- Caloric intake: slight surplus to support hypertrophy if body composition goals include fat-free mass gain; if body recomposition is the goal, aim for maintenance with weekly adjustments +/- 200–300 kcal based on progress.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day depending on sweat rate.
- Supplements: whey or vegan protein, creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (consistent daily intake), possibly omega-3s if dietary intake is low. BCAAs not necessary if protein targets are met.

Recovery modalities
- Deload weeks (Weeks 4, 8, and optionally 12 have deloads): reduce volume by 40–50% and intensity by 10–20%.
- Mobility: 10–15 minutes of mobility work post-workout targeting hips, hamstrings, shoulders, thoracic spine.
- Soft tissue work: self-myofascial release (foam roller) 2–3 times per week, especially on lower back, hip flexors, quads.

Assessment and progression metrics
- Track 1RM or estimated 1RM for squat, bench, and deadlift at baseline (Week 0) and Week 12.
- Body composition: measure around waist, hips, and maybe body fat if feasible with DXA/BWT scale; take photos monthly.
- Performance: track weekly loads for main lifts, pace of progression, and perceived exertion.

Notes about OCP and cycle effects
- The user has minimal withdrawal bleeds; no cycle-related contraindications for training intensity.
- If any menstrual cycle related fluctuations become noticeable (e.g., stronger fatigue), adjust access or volume temporarily; otherwise, maintain plan.

Customization tips
- If the client progresses faster, consider increasing weekly volume by 1–2 sets on main lifts across Weeks 6–8.
- If new to some lifts, prioritize technique and consider substituting with machines for safer form early (e.g., leg press, assisted pull-ups).
- If schedule changes, you can compress 4 days into 3 by combining big lifts with supersets, but ensure adequate recovery.

Deliverable summary for your client
- 12-week plan with 4 training days per week, progressively increasing intensity and volume across Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4 Accumulate), Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8 Intensify), Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12 Peak/Consolidate).
- Each week includes main lifts, sets/reps, and accessory movements; deload weeks integrated (Weeks 4, 8, and 12 optional tapered approach).
- Nutrition and recovery guidelines included to support strength gains and body composition improvements.

If you’d like, I can tailor the exact weekly split (e.g., Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri vs Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun), adjust exercises to equipment on hand, or convert this into a week-by-week spreadsheet with daily sets/reps and RPE targets.
